entities.name: No stage-two protocol
observations: Available searches found no study specifically validating hex-driver retention during stage-two implant uncovering; evidence is indirect.

entities.name: Dental retention measures
observations: A dental review identifies rubber dam, gauze throat screens, and floss ligatures as preventive measures for accidental ingestion or aspiration.
Extra caution is advised for supine or semi-recumbent patients.

entities.name: Pragmatic precautions
observations: An orthodontic review reports no clear evidence-based prevention guidelines and supports practical precautions as risk reduction rather than a validated protocol.

entities.name: Dental dam implant use
observations: A case report describes dental-dam use during implant placement to reduce risk from dropped implant screwdrivers, cover screws, or abutments; applicability to stage-two uncovering is indirect.

entities.name: Floss tether
observations: A securely attached floss ligature or approved tether is a simple retention precaution for a small implant driver, but must not interfere with engagement, torque, sterility, or create entanglement risk.

entities.name: Gauze throat screen
observations: A large, retrievable gauze barrier may serve as a secondary backstop when safely feasible; it is not an airway seal and should not replace direct control or tethering.

entities.name: Dental dam barrier
observations: A dental dam may provide a physical barrier when anatomy and access permit, but posterior or edentulous implant sites may make it impractical.

entities.name: Knee arthrocentesis
observations: The superolateral approach enters just lateral and superior to the patella into the suprapatellar pouch, usually with the knee extended or minimally flexed.
EULAR evidence review reports this as the most common blind approach with pooled accuracy of 91% (95% CI 84–99%).

entities.name: Superolateral knee approach
observations: For adult knee aspiration or intra-articular injection, the most precise general-purpose blind approach is superolateral: lateral/superior to the patella with the knee extended or minimally flexed.
This matches answer choice I: lateral to the patella with the knee in extension.
